description:
young_budget is min(old live, SIZE_TABLE's last entry ~7 MiB). Baseline telemetry (1d61f3742, scratch 9x7-11/tel4): dist-full median old at a minor 230 MB, cap binds at 94% of 855 minors, minors promote 481 MB, 14 majors copy 648 MB; dist-p28000 cap binds 65%, enum 37%; no other workload reaches the cap. OTP's young heap is at least its last usage, unbounded. Proposal page (approved 2026-11-17): https://claude.ai/artifact/GuEvNK64ZNHh8gDEQkMF3m (Proposal B, step 2). Interacts with fz-9x7.12 (exact-size blocks above the table stay resident on macOS): the larger young tip is such a block, and that cost is part of what each arm measures.

Experiment first, pre-registered: arms B0 today (7 MiB), B1 32 MiB cap, B2 128 MiB cap, B3 uncapped (young = old live), bench host, 25 runs (9 dist-full).
Predictions: dist-full B3 minors 855 -> <60, minor copied bytes -30%+, instructions -3%+, peak RSS up by up to ~230 MB; dist-p28000/enum smaller versions; workloads where the cap never binds within 0.5% instructions on every arm.
Pass rule: (1) an arm passes if dist-full or dist-p28000 cycles CI upper < 0.98 with peak RSS up <= 10% on every workload; (2) no workload cycles CI lower > 1.02; report the distiller's cycles-vs-RSS curve over B0-B3 regardless.

Done when (if an arm passes): young_budget's cap is the passing arm's (or gone), its doc comment states the measured reason; tests pin the budget; docs updated; full gate green. If none passes: result recorded, closure proposed to the user.
title: The young generation's size follows the live data, not the largest pooled block
